item.title: Nigeria’s Tinubu Rolls Out Cost-of-Living Plan Ahead of Election
item.description: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu unveiled a series of campaign promises ahead of January elections to ease the high cost of living, which join other measures his government has rolled out to attract voters.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Olurounbi

item.title: Italy’s Exit Tax on Wealth Needs Amendment, Meloni Ally Says
item.description: Giorgia Meloni’s push to tax wealthy people leaving Italy must be altered to not dissuade investors, a key figure in the prime minister’s coalition warned.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini and Chiara Albanese

item.title: South Africa’s ANC to Review Coalition Ties After Voting Setback
item.description: South Africa’s biggest political party will consider whether to end its national coalition with its main rival after suffering its worst electoral performance yet, an argument that’s emerging as a fault line in the race to succeed President Cyril Ramaphosa.
item.dc:creator: S'thembile Cele

item.title: Iran Hardens Line Against Nuclear Monitoring in Report to IAEA
item.description: Iran said it’s not obliged to submit to full nuclear monitoring while under threat from US military attacks, hardening its position against international inspectors.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tirone

item.title: Congress Returns With Long To-Do List As Trump Preps for Battle
item.description: Both parties are gearing up for a rocky ride heading toward the end of the year.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tamari

item.title: Democrats Risk Misreading Midterm Landslide, Trubowitz Says
item.description: Leslie Vinjamuri, CEO of the Chicago Council on Global Affairs, and Peter Trubowitz, Professor of International Relations at the London School of Economics, discuss what the Democrats’ midterm landslide means for President Donald Trump and the balance of power in Washington. They joined "The Pulse with Francine Lacqua" and examined the risks of Democrats focusing too heavily on investigations, the pressure to deliver on affordability, Trump’s legacy agenda and why AI regulation could emerge as a major issue ahead of the 2028 election. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Spy Saga Adds Roadblock to Rapid AI Advance
item.description: Jensen Huang’s admission of an affair has ramifications for politics and technology alike.
item.dc:creator: Alan Crawford

item.title: Successor Must Follow Lagarde's Approach: Nadia Calviño
item.description: Nadia Calviño, President of the European Investment Bank, joins Bloomberg's Oliver Crook on Bloomberg's "The Opening Trade" to discuss the race to succeed Christine Lagarde at the ECB, how the US midterm elections may impact Europe, and the latest on European technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Philippines VP Duterte Gets Turn in Fight for Political Survival
item.description: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial resumed on Monday after a month-long break, with attention shifting to her defense team’s strategy to avoid a guilty verdict that could end her political career.
item.dc:creator: Cliff Venzon

item.title: Hasina Seeks Passport in Step Toward Return to Bangladesh
item.description: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh’s ousted former prime minister, has asked the government to issue her a new passport and national identity card, a move that could facilitate her return more than two years after she fled to India following a mass uprising.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen

item.title: This Is How New York City Takes Out Its Trash
item.description: According to Joshua Goodman, trash collection in New York is one of the last services the city offers that is not yet touched by neoliberalism. What he means is that it's the last free and unlimited city service — there is no opt-in; it is not means tested. Goodman — who is the DSNY's deputy commissioner for public affairs and customer experience — tells us that the city deals with 24 million pounds of trash every day, and on today's podcast, he explains the logistical dance required to sort through all that garbage. We also get into why NYC produces less trash than you might think, the DSNY's new containerization program (and the new side-loading trucks they built in less than 18 months), and why recycling is not a scam. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Strikes Unlikely as Rubio Slams Iran’s Demands
item.description: US President Donald Trump struck a more conciliatory tone about Iran over the weekend, saying it’s “highly unlikely” he will order extensive strikes on the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Elimam, Eric Martin and Fiona MacDonald

item.title: Sweden Enters Decisive Phase in Negotiations to Form Government
item.description: The knots that had held Sweden’s government formation static for the past eight weeks since a tight election are unraveling fast.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: Nvidia Shares Fall As Huang's Affair Triggers China Spying Probe
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Berlin, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang admitted he had an affair with a woman identified in a series of reports as a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chip colossus into a crisis like none before in its three-decade history.
Stocks began the week on a more solid footing after dip buyers boosted US equities on Friday and Taiwan joined the ranks of Asian authorities seeking to restore investor confidence.
And Crédit Agricole has proposed a merger between Banco BPM and Crédit Agricole Italia to create Italy’s third-largest banking group, according to statement.
Today's guest: Daniela Hathorn, Capital.com, Senior Market Analyst. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Thai PM Meets Israeli Envoy, Says All Foreigners Are Treated Equally
item.description: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul met with Israel’s ambassador for talks in Bangkok, days after he revoked the citizenship of a Jewish rabbi as part of the government’s widening crackdown on illegal foreign-run businesses and misbehaving tourists.
item.dc:creator: Patpicha Tanakasempipat

item.title: China Calls Accusations It Spied on Nvidia CEO Baseless ‘Smears’
item.description: Beijing dismissed allegations that it spied on Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, an episode that is spiraling a little over a week before a meeting between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Japan, Vietnam Agree to Boost Economic Security, Energy Ties
item.description: Japan and Vietnam agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, technology, defense and energy security as their leaders met in Tokyo on Monday, seeking to strengthen economic and strategic ties amid rising regional geopolitical and trade tensions.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Dieu Tu Uyen and Sakura Murakami

item.title: Eisenkot Faces Tough Odds in Quest to Form Israeli Coalition
item.description: Former Israeli general Gadi Eisenkot faces a daunting test as he tries to cobble together a ruling coalition from a divided opposition while potentially luring allies away from Benjamin Netanyahu, a master political tactician and veteran of national power struggles.
item.dc:creator: Galit Altstein

item.title: Merz Officially Backs Aigner as Germany’s First Female President
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz backed Bavarian Ilse Aigner to become Germany’s first female president, saying the country needs a head of state supported by the political center to counter a surge for parties on the fringes.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs

item.title: South African Cities Face Coalition Rule as Voters Spurn ANC
item.description: South African political parties intensified coalition negotiations following the announcement of the results from municipal elections that produced no outright winner in seven of the eight biggest cities and saw a further weakening in support for the African National Congress.
item.dc:creator: S'thembile Cele
